title and abstract.summary: The study investigated how habitat fragmentation (connectivity and fragment size) and flower availability (abundance and species richness) affect the functional traits (social habit, body size, feeding preference, and nesting location) of wild bees and wasps within 30 natural forest-steppe fragments in the Hungarian Great Plain region.

methods.summary: The study sampled wild bee and wasp communities across 30 forest-steppe fragments in the Hungarian Great Plain, identifying species and surveying associated flower abundance and richness. The study analyzed functional traits (body size, social habit, larvae feeding preference, and nest location) for wild bees and wasps, but excluded Apis mellifera from the analyses. The study collected wasps from forest steppe study sites and gathered information on their species functional traits.
